string-array.name: faq_answers
string-array.item: Lykon Shield is a local VPN-based ad-blocker designed to block ads, tracking domains, and protect your privacy on Android devices.
It runs a local DNS server through Android\'s VPN API. It inspects DNS queries and sinks known advertisement and tracking domains locally.
No, because the VPN is completely local and does not route traffic to a remote server. The overhead is extremely low.
Bypass Apps are apps you select that will bypass the VPN entirely. Their traffic will go straight to the network without ad-blocking.
Absolutely not. All traffic stays entirely on your device. Lykon Shield does not have external trackers or cloud servers for analytics.
You can customize bypass settings and features under Developer Options or Shield System settings on the main screen.

YouTube serves ads from the same servers as actual video content, making it impossible to block them purely via DNS without blocking the videos themselves. We recommend using YouTube in a browser with ad-blocking extensions or using dedicated alternative clients.

If you experience device lag, go to Developer Options and disable \'Custom Shaders\' or set the \'Backdrop Blur Radius\' to Off. You can also exclude resource-heavy apps in the Bypass Apps configuration.

Lykon Shield blocks ad domains across most streaming and OTT applications. However, some providers stream ads directly from their primary media servers, which DNS blockers cannot filter without disrupting playback.
Some apps use encrypted DNS (DoH/DoT) to bypass local DNS settings, or fetch ads via static IP addresses. Clearing the target app\'s cache and restarting it under protection can help resolve this.
Lykon Shield is owned by the organization ProjectArcade/ and was developed by Abhinav Thakur. The project is open-source and dedicated to privacy-first community utility.
Absolutely not. Lykon Shield operates completely locally on your device. None of your DNS query logs, traffic data, credentials, or personal information ever leave your device.

Lykon Shield is built entirely out of passion and a belief in a privacy-first web. The developers earn nothing from this app directly; it is supported by volunteer contributions and open-source donation platforms.

Yes, absolutely. Who else spends weeks writing high-performance local VPN engines and complex AGSL liquid glass shaders just to give it away for free with zero ads or tracking? A financial genius would never.
The liquid glass effects are created by Kyant and are available at https://github.com/Kyant0/AndroidLiquidGlass/ under the Apache-2.0 license.
Developer has no money to publish it :(
Yes, Lykon Shield is fully open-source and hosted on GitHub under the GPL-3.0 license. The source code is owned by the organization ProjectArcade.
You can support the project by contributing code, reporting bugs on our official repository, or sharing Lykon Shield with your family and friends.
No. Lykon Shield functions purely as a DNS resolver/blocker. It only filters domain name requests (like ads.example.com) and does not decrypt or inspect your actual network traffic content.
